final_answer:
The four primary cell types — human aortic smooth muscle cells (AoSMCs), dermal fibroblasts, skeletal muscle myoblasts (SkMMs), and melanocytes — show perfectly distinct baseline transcriptional signatures, with an adjusted Rand index of 1.00 between unsupervised k-means clusters (k=4) and the known cell-type labels. Each of the 192 DMSO-treated baseline samples (48 per cell type) maps exclusively to its own cluster with 100% purity; there is no overlap.

Among the four, dermal fibroblasts and skeletal muscle myoblasts are the most similar pair (PCA centroid distance = 116.3; pseudobulk Pearson r = 0.739 on 5,000 most variable genes). AoSMCs are intermediate in similarity, closer to the fibroblast–myoblast group than to melanocytes. Melanocytes are the most transcriptionally divergent cell type, showing the largest centroid distances to all others (149.9–157.3) and the lowest pseudobulk correlations (r = 0.473–0.543 with other cell types on HVGs).

These results validate the GDPx2 primary cell screening platform: baseline transcriptional signatures are sufficiently distinct that unsupervised clustering recovers cell-type identity without error, establishing a clean background against which compound-induced transcriptional perturbations can be profiled.
grader_notes: The agent correctly identifies the 192-sample DMSO subset and achieves perfect clustering, but fails to document key preprocessing steps, uses PCA instead of TruncatedSVD, misattributes transcriptional similarity, and omits limitations. Source reliability is moderate.
